proofs.full_local_argument: Near zero W is identically 1; away from zero its defining formula is smooth, including the plateau/support boundaries since chi is globally smooth. Thus W and phi_r are C-infinity. W is strictly positive: it is a convex combination of 1 and t^(-2) for nonzero t. For |u|<=r the entire interval between 1 and u lies in [-r,r], so W(v/r)=1; integrating 120(v^3-v^2) gives 30u^4-40u^3+10. For |u|>=2r, W(u/r)=r^2/u^2, giving the tail derivative. In general phi_r'=120u^2(u-1)W(u/r), negative on (-infinity,1) except at isolated u=0, and positive on (1,infinity). Its integral over any nontrivial subinterval of (-infinity,1) is strictly negative, so 1 is the unique minimizer; the core gives all stated values. Set A3(v)=v^3W(v), A2(v)=v^2W(v). These are smooth and outside [-2,2] equal v and 1. Therefore every positive-order derivative is bounded. Differentiating phi_r'=120[r^3 A3(u/r)-r^2 A2(u/r)] q times gives sup bound 120[r^(3-q)||A3^q||_infinity+r^(2-q)||A2^q||_infinity]<=C_q r^(3-q), where C_q=120(||A3^q||_infinity+||A2^q||_infinity), using r>=1. For a continuously differentiable scalar function with bounded derivative, the mean value theorem gives Lip<=sup derivative and difference quotients give the reverse inequality. Finally u phi_r'(u)>=0 outside (0,1). Inside (0,1) it is -120u^3(1-u); differentiation shows the maximum of 120u^3(1-u) is 405/32 at u=3/4. This proves the radial bound.

statement.conclusion: phi_r is C-infinity; phi_r(u)=30u^4-40u^3+10 for |u|<=r; phi_r'(u)=120r^2(u-1) for |u|>=2r. The unique global minimizer is u=1 with inf phi_r=0; phi_r(0)=10 and phi_r'(0)=phi_r'(1)=0. ||phi_r^(q+1)||_infinity=Lip(phi_r^q)<=C_q r^(3-q). For all u, u phi_r'(u)>=-405/32.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Fix even chi in C-infinity(R;[0,1]), chi=1 for |t|<=1 and chi=0 for |t|>=2. W(t)=chi(t)+(1-chi(t))t^(-2) for t!=0, W(0)=1. For r>=1 let phi_r(u)=120 integral_1^u v^2(v-1)W(v/r)dv.
statement.parameter_domains: u in R; r>=1; integer q>=1, each fixed finite.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such fixed cutoff and r>=1, deterministically for every real u. For every integer q>=1 there exists a finite C_q depending on q and the cutoff, independent of r.
